The Zr46Ti13Nb26Ta10.5Sn4.5 (at pct) alloy was produced by vacuum arc melting using high-purity metals (purity over 99.9 wt pct) under a Ti-gettered argon atmosphere.
Rodlike samples with a diameter of ~ 10 mm and a length of ~ 60 mm were produced using the copper mold pouring technique in a high-purity argon atmosphere.
The cylindrical bar specimens were sealed in vacuum quartz tubes and homogenized at 1400 °C for 6 h, followed by water quenching.

the as-homogenized alloy was annealed at 600 °C to 1000 °C for 24 h and 600 °C for 120 h, respectively. All annealing treatments that were performed on the as-homogenized alloy were followed by water quenching to retain the phases formed at the annealing temperatures.

the as-homogenized alloy was annealed at 600 °C to 1000 °C for 24 h and 600 °C for 120 h, respectively. All annealing treatments that were performed on the as-homogenized alloy were followed by water quenching to retain the phases formed at the annealing temperatures.
The as-homogenized alloy was then annealed at 800 °C and 1000 °C for 24 h to investigate the phase stability at these temperatures.
